title: SQL Order By — Sorting with Two Keys
short_description: Produce a clean directory of users sorted for a printed roster.
detailed_description: Today you’re learning that sorting often requires more than one key. A database will only sort by what you explicitly request. If two rows tie on the first sort key, you must provide a second key to guarantee a stable order.

objectives.title: Query executes successfully
objectives.why: The database must be able to parse and run your query.

objectives.title: Use ORDER BY clause
objectives.text: Sort results using an ORDER BY clause
objectives.why: Sorting is required for this quest.

objectives.title: Multi-key Ordering
objectives.text: Sort by city ASC, then name ASC
objectives.why: We need stable ordering within each city.

objectives.title: Correct Columns
objectives.text: Return city and name in that order
objectives.why: The spec requires precisely these two columns.
